name: BURFORD CAPITAL LTD

priced.reason: book method needs rotce_override or final_growth

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That I am refusing the single most asymmetric thing in today's ten for the fifth time, and that the refusal has cost real money as the facts moved my way. Since the 2026-10-02 pass the price has fallen from $3.82 to $3.56 (-7%) while tangible book per share ROSE from $3.12 to $3.25 (+4%) and the company retired $100M of debt — so on observable book the name has got about 11% cheaper, and it is now trading at roughly 1.1x a book that has already absorbed a $2.4bn write-off. On top of that sits a contingent entitlement of roughly $700M, about 90% of the market capitalisation, which the market is pricing at approximately nothing. 'The market assigns nothing to a $1.4bn claim on a company trading at book' is the literal shape of a mispricing, and a model that refuses every time is not a model, it is an abstention.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: A ruling on Apple's judgment-as-a-matter-of-law motion, and the carrying value Burford assigns the Taction-related asset in the FY2026 10-K — the first balance-sheet date after the verdict. Also whether realisations continue at the pace of the post-quarter 12x, visible in cash receipts rather than in fair-value marks.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Three things, and all three point against the counter. (i) The market's own answer: the shares are DOWN 17.6% over the 63 days that contain the verdict — the verdict landed 2026-09-25, almost exactly 63 trading sessions before the price date — so the market has DE-RATED the equity since a judgment nominally worth 90% of its market capitalisation. (ii) Management's financing behaviour: on 2026-09-17 Burford refinanced 6.250% UNSECURED notes into 8.000% senior SECURED notes, paying 175bp more and granting security over substantially all issuer assets and subsidiary stock, in the same month as the verdict. That is not how a balance sheet about to receive $700M behaves, and it is a cheaper read on the claim's expected value than any model. (iii) Burford's own precedent, quantified in this quarter's own filing: $2.4bn of capital provision loss on one appellate ruling.
devils_advocate.unresolved: I could not value the Taction entitlement in either direction, and nothing free will let me — the case is confidential as to Burford's terms, the entitlement is subject to 'the terms of its financing agreement and applicable fees, expenses, taxes and other deductions', and the company explicitly disclaims any obligation to update. I also could not determine whether the Kilman appointment signals a contemplated structural transaction; the chairman's own framing ('capital, balance sheets and M&A for companies like Burford') on a board that has fully turned over since 2020 is suggestive and no more. Neither gap changes the verdict, because the verdict is a refusal to price, not a claim about which way the claim resolves.

what_changed: Q3 10-Q filed 2026-11-04. Tangible book value attributable to Burford Capital Limited per ordinary share is $3.25 at 2026-09-30 against $10.57 at 2025-12-31, printed side by side in the company's own non-GAAP reconciliation. Nine-month net loss attributable to BCL shareholders is $1,606,508k, including a $2.4bn capital provision loss on the YPF Judgment Reversal, partly offset by a $122.6M reversal of long-term incentive compensation accrual. Q3 itself was +$23.4M of net income, and management notes total revenues of $135M 'would have been well over $200 million if not for the non-cash increase in market discount rates'. $100M of de-leveraging in the quarter, nearest-term maturity retired, over half a billion of cash on hand ($463.8M cash plus $377.1M short-term investments). After the quarter, $64M of cash from a 2015-vintage matter at a 12x return. On the Taction Technology v. Apple verdict announced 2026-09-25 ($5.7bn jury award, Burford entitlement $1.4bn if paid as is, roughly half on balance sheet), nothing has resolved; Apple's judgment-as-a-matter-of-law motion and Federal Circuit review are still ahead. Governance: 2026-11-23 appointment of Jim Kilman (former Vice Chairman of Investment Banking at Morgan Stanley, Burford's own interim CFO 2019-21) as a non-executive director effective 2027-01-01, completing a full board turnover since 2020, with the chairman framing it as 'capital, balance sheets and M&A for companies like Burford'.
consensus_case: At $3.56 against tangible book of $3.25 a share, Burford trades at about 1.10x tangible book, not the 0.34x the brief prints. The market's case is simple and it is mostly about what tangible book IS. Burford's equity fell from $2,448.0M at 2025-12-31 to $847.955M at 2026-09-30 because the Second Circuit's 2026-03-27 reversal of the YPF/Petersen judgment produced a capital provision loss the 10-Q sizes at $2.4 billion for the nine months. What is left is $713.952M of tangible book that is itself a portfolio of fair-value marks on binary legal claims, carried behind $2,300.1M of debt including $300M of 8.000% senior SECURED notes issued 2026-09-17 against substantially all issuer assets. The equity is roughly 27% of the enterprise, so a few points of mark on the asset portfolio is tens of per cent of the equity. The market pays about book for that and no more, and its reasoning is Burford's own precedent: the YPF asset went from $2.6bn of carrying value to $160.4M on one appellate ruling.
base_case_rationale: No valuation is recordable and the printed gap is entirely defect. This is the SIXTH consecutive brief, and the FIFTH research pass, on which this name has been served the identical tangible_book_per_share of $10.538 (2026-09-07, 09-15, 09-22, 10-02 and today). justified_pb computes _tce_at(0) from equity_series[0] rather than equity_now: ($2,448,022k - $134,020k goodwill) / 219,595,601 shares = $10.538, which is the 2025-12-31 figure and reconciles exactly to Burford's own disclosed $10.57. On equity_now it is ($847,955k - $134,003k) / 219,595,601 = $3.251, which reconciles exactly to the company's own disclosed $3.25. So actual price-to-tangible-book is 1.095x against the engine's own justified 1.02 — about 7% RICH, not +203.3% cheap — and the 98th-percentile rank of 335 Financials is an artifact. The engine's equity_concept is StockholdersEquity, parent-only, so the $660,196k of non-controlling interests sitting separately on the balance sheet must NOT be deducted; that is the MFIN rule and it is why the honest figure is $3.25 and not lower. Second, independently disqualifying: unstable_rotce_2.7%_to_28.3% is raised, and per the standing EBC rule an unstable ROTCE disqualifies the model output rather than cautioning about it. The 28.3% year is the pre-reversal YPF mark and the 2.7% year is its aftermath; averaging them describes a company that no longer exists. This is the JXN condition in its purest form — GAAP net income is not a return for anything whose earnings are a mark, and management says so itself when it attributes a $65M revenue shortfall to a move in discount rates. Third, and the reason no number is honest even with both fixed: the deciding variable is whether a $5.7bn jury verdict survives post-trial motions and the Federal Circuit, on a claim whose balance-sheet half is roughly $700M against a $781.8M market capitalisation.
key_risks: The deciding input - tangible book - has been wrong in the engine in the identical way for six consecutive briefs and will be wrong again next week unless justified_pb is changed to read equity_now
